dossier.public_summary: The 1.39-day dip lines up exactly with the star's own spot rotation period and shows a light-curve swing outside the dips almost as large as the dips themselves. Centroid shows the dip is on the target, so it is not a background eclipsing binary, but a stellar binary or spot-induced signal on the M dwarf is a much better match than a 3.9-Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Out-of-transit swing has amplitude almost equal to transit depth and very high chi2, inconsistent with a planet and typical of stellar variability/spotted binary at this period.

Dip period is essentially identical to the star's spot rotation period (signal_over_rotation 0.9984229390681004) with extremely significant modulation (~4% of flux), indicating the signal is rotation-driven variability folded at the photometric period, not an independent transit.

reasons.check: duration.ratio vs transit shape and fit density
reasons.why: Transit is too long for a central transit of this 0.382 Rsun M-dwarf, and density penalty dominates the fit despite a flat-bottom look, supporting a spot/EB interpretation over a planet which would require a much higher density star.
